title: 2026 Managing Director
description:
**Who we are:**

United We Dream (UWD) is the largest immigrant youth-led community in the country. We create welcoming spaces for young people – regardless of immigration status – to support, engage, and empower them to make their voices heard and win!

With an online reach of over 5 million every month, more than 1,000,000 members as well as 4 statewide branches and local groups across 28 states. UWD is made up of fearless young people fighting to improve the lives of our members and their families. Our vision is a society which celebrates our diversity and believes in a multi-ethnic, intersectional path to getting there. Over 60% of our members are womxn and 30% identify as LGBTQ.

We are driven by the priorities and needs of our members; have trained thousands of individuals; and have supported countless local organizing groups. Our grassroots-driven approach has a proven record of success and we’re looking for talented folks to join our team!

Learn more about United We Dream by visiting www.unitedwedream.org.

**Position Summary**

United We Dream is seeking a new senior leader and organization-builder to serve in the role of Managing Director. In partnership with the Executive Director, the Managing Director will develop and drive an organizational strategy to maximize UWD’s assets including its people power, brand, as well as financial and operational resources, to build the power necessary to change the lives of our members, leaders and communities.

We are looking for an experienced, strategic, insightful, and mission-driven leader who thrives on creating and managing systems and community in service to an organization’s mission. As the primary thought partner to the Executive Director (ED), the Managing Director translates the organization’s vision into seamless, cohesive execution across five core pillars: 1) long-term organizational strategic vision; 2) financial sustainability & growth strategy; 3) operations strategy responsive to the needs of a fast-paced community power building infrastructure; 4) organizational security and compliance strategy; and 5) organizational structure and culture that successfully drives organizational priorities.

This position works with all members of the internal leadership, including leading the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team, and will coordinate internal processes across departments to cultivate and maintain an effective team, a commitment to excellence, and healthy organizational culture.

A successful candidate will be passionate about UWD’s mission and be highly motivated to work in a fast-growing, front-line, history-making organization. They must be committed to leadership development, power building, and building collaborative structures which make the most of a highly talented staff team.

This is a full-time exempt position. Much day-to-day work will be handled remotely, but travel (local, nation-wide, international) is expected for approximately 30-40% of the time. Applicants working in the eastern time zone are preferred but not required. Multilingual communication skills are a plus though not required.

**Primary Responsibilities**

### **Long-Term Organizational Strategy & Leadership Alignment**

* Strategic Thought Partner: Serves as thought partner to the Executive Director on all aspects of organizational strategy including programs, internal operations and team management, growth, and brand.
* Strategic Planning: Lead the development, rollout, and regular evaluation of the multi-year organizational strategic vision in partnership with the Executive Director, Senior Leadership Team, and Board of Directors.
* Execution & Accountability: Lead the Executive Team, the Senior Leadership Team, and the Staff through annual goal setting, translating the organization’s long-term vision into ambitious but realizable organizational goals that build year after year
  + Works with the Senior Leadership Team to arrive at Department-Level goals that will implement the organizational goals
  + Leads periodic stepbacks with the SLT and the Staff to assess progress made on goals as well as any changes that need to be made
* Internal Leadership:

* Provides day-to-day management of the Executive Team and the Senior Leadership Team and ensures that the teams are high functioning, collaborative and effective leadership bodies.
  + Lead ET and SLT meetings and stepback spaces
* Oversees planning and execution of all-staff and all-leadership gatherings and retreats.
* Staffs the Executive Director in internal settings or speaks on their behalf in internal settings when required.
* Serves as the chief of internal communications, crafting and/or approving internal communications materials related to United We Dream’s organizational effectiveness.
* Supports the Executive Director to ensure the achievement of key internal culture and operations goals.
* Board Management:
  + Work with the Executive Director and Co-Chairs of the Board to lead board meetings and relevant board committee meetings
  + Prepare high-level briefings and strategic board materials
  + Facilitate alignment at Executive Committee meetings.
* Special Projects: Direct priority high-stakes or rapid-response projects and incubates initiatives from concept to handoff or implementation.

### **Financial Sustainability & Growth Strategy**

* Supervise the Senior Director of Finance and Development
* Revenue Strategy Collaboration: Partner with the Senior Director of Finance and Development to strategize around and execute long-term revenue diversification strategies, including major gifts, institutional funding, earn-income models, and rapid-response campaign fundraising.
* Resource Allocation: Partner with the Senior Director of Finance and Development to ensure strategic priorities are directly linked to annual budgeting and financial forecasting analysis, optimizing resource allocation for maximum programmatic impact.
* Capital & Reserve Management: Partner with the Senior Director of Finance and Development to oversee financial sustainability and growth metrics, long-term reserve and investments planning, and fiscal decision-making models to weather potential political or economic shifts.

### **Operational Strategy & Organizational Effectiveness**

* Supervise the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems.
* Oversee the contract relationship with our operations partner Seed the Dream, and create staff and consultant support systems as needed.
* Change Management:
  + Lead major organizational change initiatives or organizational redesigns
  + Partner with the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems to lead culture-building endeavors that promote courage, rigor, community, resilience, and high performance.
* Inter-Departmental Collaboration:
  + Serve as the central, high-level oversight ensuring effective coordination between all parts of the organization – the Membership and Campaigns Department, Narrative Department, Development Department, Finance Department, and the Data and Operations Department.
* Movement-Values Aligned & Effective Operations:
  + Oversees the Operations partner to ensure the complete, seamless, and values-aligned operational apparatus and set-up for programs, activities, tactics, etc.
  + Oversees the Operations partner to ensure the complete, seamless, and values-aligned planning and execution of in-person events or actions, including large scale ones with multiple external participants and partners.

### **Security, Risk Mitigation & Compliance**

* Holistic Organizational Strategy:
  + Anticipate and monitor changes in legal, regulatory and administrative environments
    - Partner with the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems to devise plans to implement changes in organizational policies/procedures as needed to maintain compliance.
    - Partner with the Adviser on Special Projects and the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems to strategize about legal risks to the organization and bring in necessary counsel
    - Partner with the Narrative Director to assess any additions to external communications strategy
  + Anticipate and monitor our organizational security needs across all aspects (physical, digital, data, reputational, etc.) and and partner with the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems to devise plans for improvements necessary to support the growth of specific programs and UWD overall;
* Legal Compliance: Ensure complete compliance across nonprofit regulatory frameworks (including 501(c)(3) / 501(c)(4) advocacy and lobbying rules, charitable registrations, etc.), maintaining proactive legal and reputational risk management policies and systems.
* Crisis Management: Develop and maintain rapid-response crisis plans, leading incident response teams during political retaliation, legal challenges, security breaches, or public relations crises.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Strengthen the culture: Partner with the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems to ensure a safe, welcoming, and inspiring organizational culture for staff to excel in. Role model and uphold UWD’s values of creating a courageous, rigorous, and community-oriented working environment.
  + Partner with the Director of Organizational Culture and Systems and with the Operations partner to develop, revise, and uphold organization policies and standards, ensuring that organizational policies are in line with the organization’s guiding principles as well as relevant compliance regulations and concerns.
* Support fundraising:Collaborate with the Executive Director and Development Department team in developing and executing a forward-thinking fundraising strategy for organizational priorities.
* Demonstrate embodied leadership:Prioritize taking care of your physical and emotional health as a key component of thriving in your role. Practice self-care behaviors in ways that work best for you and proactively encourage your staff to prioritize self-care as well. Project trust & confidence in your abilities and skills and recognize the achievements and abilities of others
* Manage organizational change:As the organization undergoes continued growth and innovation, the Managing Director will manage organizational change in a way that inspires and activates the Board, staff, members and community.

**Desired Qualifications and Skills**

* 8+ years of experience in the progressive, non-profit or movement space with a well rounded background across organizational departments.
* Well developed emotional intelligence and communication skills, is able to build trusting relationships with a wide array of individuals
* A critical thinker and a capable, flexible, curious generalist.
* Demonstrated experience in successfully developing and executing major, large-scale project plans involving many moving pieces and collaborators.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with an ability to understand a wide range of audiences and interests.
* Demonstrated experience in building staff teams, management, coaching and leadership development.
* The ability to build strong relationships internal to the organization and external for the organization
* Experience with seeing the long vision of an organization while understanding the importance of accomplishing short and medium term objectives.
* Experience with being able to conceptualize and approach problems and solutions in a proactive, constructive, and innovative manner that will result in improved performance across the organization.
* Strong follow through with principals and with organizers.
* A passion for the mission: We believe that those closest to the pain are the closest to the solutions, therefore a successful candidate must be “all in” on UWD being an immigrant youth-led organization

**Interpersonal Skills**

* An exceptional team player; exemplifies a work style that is committed to the excellence that our members and team deserve while being flexible, respectful, collaborative and nimble;
* Can build trust, confidence, and leadership among a diverse range of staff, fellow, partner organizations - across race, gender, and other identities

**Cultural Competency**

* Strong understanding of the immigrant experience, preferably with lived experience as an undocumented person, immigrant, or immigrant family
* Understanding of race, gender, sexuality and other aspects of identity, and their intersections, and how that plays out in the work. Experience building strong relationships and trust across race, gender, class, and other group identities, both internally and externally
* Brings an anti-racist lens to their work and understands the role that white-supremacy and anti-Blackness play in the environments in which we operate
* Demonstrates self-awareness of their own multiple group identities and their attendant dynamics, and can adapt the approach as needed
* Experience working in communities of color and/or building multiracial organizing efforts
* Knowledge of immigrants rights’ policy and organizing landscape is preferred

**Compensation**

Salary Range: $160,000.00- $180,000.00

**Benefits:**

  

* Employees who have completed less than 1 year of service with United We Dream:
  + 10 Vacation days per year
* Employees who have completed more than 1 year of service but less than 3 with United We Dream:
  + 12 Vacation days per year
* Employees who have completed more than 3 years of service but less than 5 with United We Dream:
  + 17 Vacation days per year
* Employees who have completed more than 5 years of service with United We Dream:
  + 22 Vacation days per year
* Paid two weeks Off Holiday between December and January.
* 12 Paid holidays
* 4% 403(B) employer discretionary contribution
* 12 weeks of paid family leave (after 1 and 1 day of service)
* Medical/Dental/Vision/Life coverage
* $120 Reimbursement included cell service/data and utilities monthly
* $500 Reimbursement for office supplies working from home annually
* $2000 Stipend towards professional development

**To Apply**

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Please submit a cover letter, resume, at least one writing example, and salary requirement via email to **humanresources@unitedwedream.org** and include **Managing Director (LAST NAME, FIRST NAME)** in the subject line. Please do not send duplicate materials and incomplete applications will not be considered. No phone calls, please.

###

UWD is an equal opportunity employer; people of color and individuals from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. UWD does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ethnic background, citizenship status, religion, political orientation, genetic information, sexual orientation, age or disability.

title: Marketing Director
description:
Excellent creative work can help extraordinary organizations raise more and serve more. Unseen is looking for a Marketing Director who knows what great looks like, can explain why it works, and can bring together the people who make it happen.

You will own Unseen's brand, voice, marketing strategy, and creative standard. You will lead an outside agency through a brand rebuild, turn that work into a focused annual marketing plan, and direct major projects for selected Unseen partners.

You will turn complex information into compelling ideas that capture attention, build belief, and motivate action. You will set creative direction and hold teams accountable for quality.

Creating amazing products and campaigns is the floor. Activating people to invest in anti trafficking work is the job.

About Unseen

Unseen accelerates the fight against human trafficking and its root causes. We equip anti-trafficking organizations around the world with marketing, fundraising, and storytelling tools, and we deliver strategic grants that fund their most critical projects.

Since 2011, Unseen has worked with 94 partner organizations in 66 countries. Those partners have raised more than $119 million and served more than 1.3 million people.

We are entering a new chapter and investing in the leadership and creative work to support it.

The opportunity

This is a role for someone whose strength is creative judgment and leadership. You can recognize an exceptional idea, write a clear brief, give specific feedback, and push work further. You know how to recruit talented people and hold them to a high standard.

You will have direct access to Unseen's leadership, room to challenge assumptions, and the opportunity to shape work with lasting consequences. We want someone who can push back on the CEO's preferences, support their recommendations, and earn trust through their decisions.

You will lead through strategy, direction, and accountability, not by personally producing every asset. A social media specialist will activate the social strategy, and a production manager and production team will manage the execution of creative projects. You will guide the standard of work, help identify outside talent, and collaborate with the people responsible for daily delivery.

What you will lead

Brand and voice. Serve as the primary day-to-day client for an outside brand agency, guide the rebuild, and establish standards the team can consistently apply.

Marketing strategy. Build and execute an annual plan with clear audiences, priorities, budgets, responsibilities, and measures of success. Define how marketing builds awareness and trust, motivates engagement, and supports measurable growth.

Visibility and credibility. Build Unseen's visibility and credibility among priority donors and businesses, activating established relationships and advocates in selected markets.

Fundraising communications. Set the strategy and creative direction for campaigns, stories, and materials that support philanthropic strategy, major gifts, Guardian Business expansion, and a major capital initiative.

Partner projects. Lead strategic and creative oversight for substantial marketing and storytelling assignments for selected Unseen partners, with scope and delivery commitments established through the annual plan.

Creative talent. Identify, evaluate, recruit, and brief excellent agencies, freelancers, and other creative specialists.

Quality and accountability. Set creative standards, provide decisive feedback, and remain accountable for the quality and strategic effectiveness of work delivered by staff, production teams, agencies, and contractors without directly managing every task.

Practical AI adoption. Champion thoughtful AI use in research, creative development, workflows, and production, while protecting accuracy, privacy, and storytelling integrity.

Our philanthropic leadership owns fundraising strategy, donor relationships, and asks. Our Guardian Business lead owns that program's expansion. You will be their marketing partner, responsible for work that helps them succeed.

What you bring

* Exceptional creative judgment across storytelling, copy, design, photography, video, and campaigns.
* Demonstrated ability to turn complex information into persuasive creative concepts using audience psychology, narrative tension, message hierarchy, and clear calls to action.
* A track record of developing campaigns that produce measurable results, including fundraising outcomes, with an honest account of your strategy, decisions, contribution, and results.
* Experience selecting, briefing, directing, and evaluating outside agencies and creative specialists, including providing clear feedback and knowing when to change course.
* The ability to recruit strong creative talent beyond your existing contacts.
* Clear, constructive leadership that makes other people's work better.
* Strong execution skills, including setting priorities, managing budgets, and delivering on commitments through teams.
* Resourcefulness within a limited budget, with the judgment to surface tradeoffs early and recommend solutions.
* Practical fluency with AI tools and the ability to lead adoption collaboratively.
* Respect for ethical, survivor-centered storytelling that protects dignity, informed consent, privacy, and personal agency.

An established network of creative professionals, agencies, media contacts, or business partners is a plus. Experience in anti-trafficking work is welcome but not required.

What success looks like

In your first year, you will:

* Launch Unseen's brand rebuild and establish a consistent voice and creative standard.
* Build and execute a focused annual marketing plan with defined audiences, engagement goals, and performance measures.
* Provide creative direction and quality oversight for priority campaigns and partner projects delivered by the responsible teams against agreed goals, schedules, and budgets.
* Equip our fundraising and Guardian Business teams with compelling, useful materials and evaluate how those materials support engagement and growth.
* Build a dependable bench of creative specialists and strong working relationships with production leadership.
* Improve how we evaluate creative quality, audience response, campaign performance, and team delivery.

We will establish specific milestones together based on organizational priorities and available resources.

Working at Unseen

You will report to the COO and work closely with the CEO on brand direction and creative standards. Within approved organizational priorities and brand strategy, you will lead creative recommendations and day-to-day marketing decisions.

Our team works remotely across multiple locations. This role requires regular overlap with Central Time business hours and travel for selected events. Two team meetups per year are encouraged.

The salary range is $75,000 to $95,000, depending on experience and demonstrated capabilities.

You will have flexibility, meaningful creative responsibility, access to global partners and powerful stories of hope, and the opportunity to help organizations change lives for generations.

How to apply

Please submit your resume or professional background, plus:

1. Two examples of campaigns or major creative projects you led. Include the objective, your role, the team or agency involved, approximate budget, and results. At least one should demonstrate fundraising impact.

2. A short note explaining why this opportunity interests you and what you would bring to Unseen.

3. An intro video highlighting who you are and what makes you the best fit to join this team.

Links, existing case studies, and concise summaries are welcome. You may anonymize confidential information. We are interested in the quality of your judgment and contribution, not the polish of your application.

Candidates who advance will discuss their work with our leadership team and participate in a focused creative leadership exercise.

Pay: $75,000.00 - $95,000.00 per year

Application Question(s):

* Please share two examples of campaigns or major creative projects you led. Include the objective, your role, the team or agency involved, approximate budget, and results. At least one should demonstrate fundraising impact. Links or concise summaries are welcome.
* Please write a short note explaining why this opportunity interests you and what you would bring to Unseen.
* Please include a link to a short intro video highlighting who you are and what makes you the best fit for this team.

description:
**About Trauma Healing Accelerated**

Trauma Healing Accelerated (THA) is an education organization built on the Biology of Trauma® framework developed by Dr. Aimie Apigian, a double board-certified physician and author of *The Biology of Trauma*. The framework explains how unresolved trauma is held in the body and nervous system, and how it can be addressed through a biology-first approach.

THA serves two audiences: individuals pursuing their own healing, and the coaches, therapists and clinicians who support them. Our offerings span free educational resources, including the Biology of Trauma podcast and YouTube channel, through our flagship Foundational Journey, the Biology of Trauma® modules and yearlong programs. All THA offerings are educational in nature and do not constitute medical advice.

* Position: Content & Growth Lead
* Location: Remote (team operates on Pacific Time)
* Reports to: Executive Director of Programs
* Key relationship: Dr. Aimie Apigian, Founder
* Employment type: Contract, full-time hours

**Position overview**

The Content & Growth Lead is accountable for THA's growth engine: the strategy, content and channels through which new audiences discover our work and enroll in our programs. The role holds a comprehensive command of THA's existing content library and determines what should be created, repurposed or reintroduced to market.

This is a strategic leadership position with hands-on responsibility. The Content & Growth Lead sets direction across email marketing, podcast, YouTube, social media, the website, partnerships, speaking and public relations, directs the contributors who execute that work, and owns the weekly performance reporting for each channel. The role relies on AI tools and automated systems to research, draft, repurpose and report at a scale a small team could not reach manually.

**Key responsibilities**

**Content strategy and library management**

* Maintain a thorough working knowledge of THA's content library, including podcast episodes, video, courses, workshops, guides and participant testimonials.
* Determine what content to create, repurpose or reintroduce, prioritizing what advances prospective participants toward enrollment.
* Own the integrated content and marketing calendar, aligning launches, evergreen content and promotions across all channels.
* Ensure all content reflects the founder's voice and THA brand standards, and manage the approval process with appropriate lead time.

**Email marketing**

* Lead email marketing strategy, including campaigns, launch sequences, nurture flows and list health across both audience segments.
* Plan, write or direct, test and report on all email communications.

**Channel oversight**

* **Podcast and YouTube:** Direct episode strategy, AI search-optimized titles and descriptions, and clip production that supports audience acquisition.
* **Social media:** Oversee Instagram and Facebook for the individual audience and LinkedIn for the practitioner audience, including short-form video, copy, comment automation and paid amplification of high-performing content.
* **Website:** Oversee messaging, landing pages and opt-in experiences to improve visitor-to-subscriber conversion.
* **Partnerships:** Develop podcast guest appearances, affiliate and collaborator promotions, and cross-audience partnerships.
* **Speaking and public relations:** Secure and prepare speaking engagements and media opportunities for the founder.
* **Book events:** Plan and promote in-person and virtual gatherings centered on *The Biology of Trauma* that introduce new audiences to THA.

**Team leadership and performance reporting**

* Direct the creative, video and marketing contributors who produce content, providing clear briefs and quality review prior to founder approval.
* Review weekly performance metrics for each channel, interpret results and recommend next actions.

**AI and automation**

* Use AI tools such as Claude daily to research topics, draft and edit content in the founder's voice, and repurpose long-form material into email, social and video assets.
* Design and maintain automated workflows for content production, publishing, comment automation, email sequences and weekly reporting.
* Build and refine AI assistants, prompts and brand-voice guides so contributors produce on-brand work with less review.
* Partner with THA's AI and web systems specialist to identify new opportunities to automate repetitive work.
* Review all AI-generated content for accuracy and voice before it is published.

**Key performance indicators**

Performance in this role is measured by business outcomes rather than content volume.

* Growth in email subscribers and assessment completions, by acquisition source
* Conversion from free content into the Foundational Journey and other programs
* Email performance, including open and click rates, list health and revenue per campaign
* Podcast downloads, YouTube watch time and subscriber growth, and social media reach and engagement
* Partnership, speaking and media opportunities secured each quarter
* Consistent delivery of complete, on-brand work, reducing quality issues that require founder intervention

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Demonstrated experience leading multichannel content or growth marketing, with email marketing as a core competency.
* A proven record of connecting content strategy to measurable outcomes, including subscriber growth, conversion and revenue.
* Advanced, hands-on proficiency with AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT for content research, drafting and repurposing, with examples of how AI improved output or results.

* Experience directing the work of others through clear briefs, review and constructive feedback.

No prior experience with THA programs is necessary.

title: Director of Safety
description:
Honor Technology's mission is to change the way society cares for older adults. As a leader in aging care innovation, Honor provides the technology, tools, and services that empower older adults to live life on their own terms. Honor's growing portfolio includes its consumer care brand, Home Instead, Inc., the world's leading provider of in-home care for older adults. With a global franchise network and more than 100,000 Care Pros, Home Instead delivers over 50 million hours of personalized care annually.

Together, Honor and Home Instead are setting a new standard for aging in place, backed by powerful technology, compassionate care, and a commitment to aging on your own terms.

Join us to create a new and better aging experience for our clients, their families, and our Care Professionals.

**About the Role**

We're hiring a Director of Safety to build and scale safety strategy for our distributed in-home care workforce. In this role, you will own reducing injury rates and severity, reducing workers' compensation spend, and driving a safe environment for clients and Care Professionals (CPs). You'll mine large, ambiguous, and imperfect datasets to surface the risk indicators that actually predict incidents and injuries, then design systemic solutions—built on technology, not just process—that hold up as we grow into new markets and service lines. You'll own the full workers' compensation lifecycle, building durable programs that manage costs more effectively. You will also partner with Product and Engineering to build tools and automation that make safety a scalable advantage rather than a manual, reactive function.

The right candidate has built and scaled safety, trust & safety, or risk programs inside a technology-enabled, high-growth, distributed workforce, using data and product thinking to solve problems at scale. You're equally comfortable diving into the details of a single incident investigation and stepping back to design company-wide systems. You think outside the box rather than defaulting to "industry best practice"—you can identify the handful of activities that actually move injury and cost outcomes, build the case for whichever investment they require, and influence outcomes across distributed teams who don't report to you. You can also translate messy, imperfect data into a clear, credible story for leadership.

This role is fully remote and can be based anywhere in the U.S. You'll manage your team remotely, so strong written communication and remote coaching skills are essential.

**As a Director of Safety at Honor, you will:**

**Safety Program Leadership**

* Own the safety operating model and architecture, balancing quick fixes with the larger structural changes the business needs as it scales.
* Build systemic solutions that address common in-home care hazards: environmental safety, mobility issues, infection control, client behavior, and more.
* Partner with Product and Engineering to build tools, automation, and product features that reduce risk, and make the case for the investment they require.
* Develop programs to build a culture of safety among Care Professionals and HQ employees.

**Workers' Compensation & Incident Management**

* Own the outcome of reducing workers' compensation spend, with end-to-end accountability for strategy and case management.
* Use data to find the levers that reduce claim cost and cycle time, and build durable programs and tooling that manage costs more effectively when injuries do occur, keeping claims on track at scale.
* Own vendor management and evaluate alternative models.
* Lead incident investigations and root cause analysis, and turn findings into corrective action plans that prevent recurrence.
* Maintain accurate incident records and reporting for leadership.
* Forecast reserves, build forward-looking budgets, and communicate financial impact to leadership. • Ensure compliance with OSHA and state-specific home care regulations.

**Data & Culture**

* Own the metrics that make safety and claims performance visible and enable early intervention.
* Communicate complex and imperfect data clearly to leadership, presenting findings and recommendations—including business cases for new investment—in terms executives can act on.
* Influence outcomes across distributed, cross-functional teams—franchise operators, field leaders, Product, and Engineering—who don't report to you directly.

**Leadership Principles We'll Assess in This Role**

* **Balance Incremental and Radical Change:** You know when to close the gap with a quick fix and when the data says to rethink the safety or claims model entirely. You push for durable, technology-enabled programs and you're willing to think outside the box and embrace unconventional approaches when a conventional fix won't hold.
* **Think Systemically:** You consider how a safety intervention ripples across markets, franchise operators, Care Pros, and clients before you act, and you build systemic solutions that leverage technology rather than one-off fixes. You identify the handful of activities that actually move injury rates and workers' compensation spend, rather than defaulting to "industry best practice."
* **Fly High & Dive Deep:** You work with large, ambiguous, and imperfect datasets to find the risk indicators hiding in the noise, and you know when to dive into the details of a single claim or incident versus stepping back to run the function at scale. You audit when the data and what you're hearing from the field don't match.
* **Drive Impact:** You own the outcome of reducing workers' compensation spend and building a safer environment for clients and Care Professionals—measured by injury rate and severity reduction, not activity. You communicate complex and imperfect data clearly to leadership and influence outcomes across distributed, cross-functional teams who don't report to you.

**We're Looking for You to Bring**

* 8+ years in safety, risk, trust & safety, or operations leadership, with a track record of scaling programs inside a fast-growing, technology-enabled, distributed workforce (delivery, rideshare, e-commerce fulfillment, on-demand services, logistics).
* Strong data skills (SQL, analytics, dashboarding) and a track record of working with large, ambiguous, and imperfect datasets to identify risk indicators, find root causes, and prioritize investment.
* Experience using technology and automation—not just process and headcount—to scale safety or operational outcomes.
* Experience owning workers' compensation end-to-end: claims, return-to-work plans, and provider relationships (or comparable risk/insurance claims experience).
* A track record of building the business case for investment, communicating complex and imperfect data clearly, and winning buy-in from senior leadership.
* Experience building and managing a remote team, including hiring, developing, and retaining talent as a function scales.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence outcomes across distributed teams—from frontline staff to executives.
* Working knowledge of OSHA and related regulatory frameworks, or the ability to ramp quickly from an adjacent regulated environment.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience at a technology-enabled, high-growth company (DoorDash, Amazon, Chewy, Instacart, Uber, Lyft, or similar) in safety, trust & safety, risk, or operations.
* Experience partnering with Product and Engineering to ship tools or product features that reduce risk at scale.
* Familiarity with modern safety/case management software, data platforms, and BI tools.
* Experience scaling a team through a period of significant growth, including building a leadership pipeline.

*#LI-AN1*

At Honor, we put people first. Our leadership culture is guided by Leadership Principles that prioritize integrity, compassion, and excellence. We offer a unique opportunity to lead with purpose and make a meaningful impact no matter your role.

title: Director of Marketing
description:
CyberSheath Services International LLC is a rapidly growing Managed Services Provider primarily focused on providing Cybersecurity services to the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). We are excited to be expanding our staff due to our growth and are looking to add a Director of Channel Partnerships & Business Development to our team!

CyberSheath integrates compliance and threat mitigation efforts and eliminates redundant security practices that don't improve and, in fact, may weaken an organization's security posture. Our professionals tell clients where to stop spending, where to invest, and how to take what they are already doing and integrate it in a way that delivers improved security.

Successful candidates for CyberSheath are self-motivated, think out of the box, work, and solve issues independently. Additionally, our most successful people are self-starters and willing to put on many hats in order to succeed. CyberSheath is fast-growing and seeks candidates who want to be part of our upward trajectory.

Position Overview

CyberSheath is seeking a strategic, hands-on Director of Marketing to build and lead a high-performing marketing function during a pivotal period of market growth and increasing CMMC adoption. This leader will own the development and execution of an integrated marketing strategy that strengthens brand authority, creates qualified pipeline, accelerates revenue, and positions CyberSheath as the trusted cybersecurity compliance partner for the Defense Industrial Base.

The Director of Marketing will translate complex cybersecurity, regulatory, and technical concepts into clear, credible, audience-specific messaging that resonates with executive buyers, IT and security leaders, compliance stakeholders, and operational leaders at defense contractors. This person will combine strategic rigor with operational excellence—setting the go-to-market plan while remaining close to campaigns, content, events, demand generation, performance analytics, and sales alignment.

The ideal candidate is a data-driven B2B marketing leader with experience in cybersecurity, managed services, compliance technology, government contracting, or similarly complex technical markets. They are comfortable operating in a growth-stage, private equity-backed environment, understand long sales cycles and multi-stakeholder buying committees, and know how to create measurable marketing impact.

What You'll Do

Marketing Strategy and Go-to-Market

* Develop and lead CyberSheath's annual and quarterly marketing strategy in partnership with executive leadership, sales, solution engineering, customer success, and service delivery.
* Define target segments, ideal customer profiles, buyer personas, market priorities, and account-tiering strategies for defense contractors and subcontractors navigating CMMC, DFARS, and NIST SP 800-171 requirements.
* Build integrated go-to-market plans for CyberSheath's core managed compliance, managed security, managed IT, assessment, implementation, and secure enclave offerings.
* Establish clear marketing priorities, budgets, milestones, operating cadences, and performance expectations tied to company revenue objectives.
* Identify market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and customer pain points that should inform messaging, campaigns, sales enablement, and product/service positioning.
* Support market expansion and new-service launches with disciplined positioning, audience targeting, launch planning, campaign execution, and performance measurement.

Demand Generation and Revenue Marketing

* Own the demand-generation engine from awareness through opportunity creation, working closely with Sales to drive pipeline quality, velocity, conversion, and revenue contribution.
* Create and optimize multi-channel campaigns across digital advertising, search, email nurture, webinars, content syndication, events, partner marketing, social media, and account-based marketing.
* Design programs that engage key buying-committee members, including CEOs, COOs, CFOs, CISOs, CIOs, IT leaders, compliance leaders, program managers, and operations executives.
* Partner with Sales leadership to define lead stages, service-level agreements, qualification criteria, routing processes, follow-up expectations, and closed-loop reporting.
* Build account-based marketing programs for priority accounts, strategic verticals, and high-value partner ecosystems.
* Develop nurture paths that educate prospective customers on compliance urgency, business risk, assessment readiness, remediation needs, and the operational requirements of maintaining CMMC compliance over time.
* Continuously test audience, channel, message, offer, and conversion-path hypotheses to improve marketing efficiency and pipeline outcomes.

Brand, Messaging, and Content

* Own CyberSheath's brand strategy, voice, positioning, messaging architecture, and narrative across external and internal-facing marketing assets.
* Ensure CyberSheath clearly communicates its differentiation as a specialized, end-to-end cybersecurity compliance partner for defense contractors rather than a generalist technology or security provider.
* Lead development of high-value thought leadership, including executive articles, regulatory explainers, blogs, guides, case studies, solution briefs, webinars, customer stories, analyst-facing content, and event presentations.
* Translate highly technical and regulatory subject matter into accessible, commercially relevant content without sacrificing accuracy or credibility.
* Partner with internal subject-matter experts to develop compelling perspectives on CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, secure CUI environments, managed security, assessment readiness, and continuous compliance.
* Maintain a high editorial standard and a consistent content calendar that supports organic demand, customer education, sales enablement, search visibility, and executive thought leadership.
* Oversee website messaging, conversion paths, content governance, SEO priorities, and user experience improvements.

Product and Sales Enablement

* Partner with Sales, Solution Engineering, and Service Delivery to sharpen service positioning, customer value propositions, competitive differentiation, and proof points.
* Develop sales-enablement materials such as pitch decks, battlecards, solution briefs, case studies, industry-specific messaging, objection-handling resources, and customer presentation templates.
* Equip revenue teams with clear, current, and consistent messaging for every stage of the buyer journey.
* Create mechanisms to capture and distribute market intelligence from prospects, customers, partners, competitors, and frontline revenue teams.
* Support customer marketing initiatives, including advocacy, testimonials, referral programs, case studies, and expansion campaigns.

Events, Partnerships, and Field Marketing

* Refine CyberSheath's strategy for industry events, trade shows, conferences, webinars, and executive programs relevant to the DIB, defense contracting, cybersecurity, compliance, and government technology markets.
* Ensure events are planned against measurable objectives, including target-account engagement, meeting generation, pipeline influence, partner activation, and revenue impact.
* Build co-marketing programs with strategic technology, channel, and ecosystem partners, including Microsoft and other organizations serving the compliance and defense-contractor market.
* Identify opportunities for CyberSheath executives and subject-matter experts to build visibility through speaking engagements, contributed content, media opportunities, and industry participation.

Analytics, Operations, and Team Leadership

* Establish a metrics-driven marketing operating model that measures awareness, engagement, marketing-sourced pipeline, marketing-influenced pipeline, conversion rates, customer acquisition cost, campaign ROI, pipeline velocity, and revenue contribution.
* Build and maintain reliable dashboards and executive reporting that clearly communicate marketing performance, key insights, risks, and recommended actions.
* Manage marketing technology, data hygiene, attribution, campaign operations, and budget discipline in partnership with Revenue Operations and other internal stakeholders.
* Evaluate and optimize the marketing technology stack, vendors, agencies, freelancers, and internal resources to ensure efficient execution.
* Hire, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing marketing team as the organization grows.
* Foster a collaborative, accountable, customer-centric culture that values speed, quality, experimentation, commercial impact, and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 6 to 12 months, the Director of Marketing will be expected to:

* Establish a clear, differentiated, and consistent market narrative for CyberSheath and its service portfolio.
* Implement an integrated demand-generation strategy that produces a predictable flow of qualified opportunities.
* Strengthen alignment between Marketing, Sales, Solution Engineering, and Customer Success around target accounts, lead management, messaging, and pipeline goals.
* Improve visibility into marketing performance through practical, trusted funnel and revenue reporting.
* Elevate CyberSheath's thought-leadership presence in the CMMC, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, and broader DIB cybersecurity compliance market.
* Build a scalable content engine that supports organic growth, outbound sales efforts, customer education, and partner engagement.
* Improve conversion across core marketing journeys, including website engagement, webinar registration, gated-content conversion, demo requests, assessment inquiries, and sales-accepted leads.
* Establish a repeatable field, event, and partner-marketing framework tied to measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, communications, or a related field; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* 8+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience, including 3+ years in a marketing leadership role.
* Demonstrated success developing and executing marketing strategies that drive measurable pipeline, revenue, and market growth.
* Experience marketing complex B2B services, technology solutions, cybersecurity offerings, managed services, compliance solutions, SaaS, or enterprise IT services.
* Strong command of demand generation, account-based marketing, content strategy, digital marketing, field marketing, campaign operations, and marketing analytics.
* Experience supporting sales organizations with long, complex sales cycles and multiple economic, technical, and operational stakeholders.
* Proven ability to translate technical concepts into customer-focused positioning, messaging, and content.
* Strong executive communication, presentation, writing, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Experience managing budgets, agencies, vendors, and marketing technology platforms.
* Track record of building and leading high-performing teams in fast-moving, growth-oriented environments.
* Analytical mindset and fluency with funnel metrics, attribution, conversion analysis, pipeline reporting, and campaign performance optimization.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in cybersecurity, cybersecurity compliance, managed security services, managed IT services, GRC, risk management, or regulated technology markets.
* Familiarity with the Defense Industrial Base, federal contracting, CMMC 2.0, DFARS, NIST SP 800-171, FedRAMP, CUI, or government cloud environments.
* Experience marketing to defense contractors, manufacturers, engineering firms, federal contractors, or regulated mid-market organizations.
* Experience working in a private equity-backed or high-growth business environment.
* Familiarity with CRM, marketing automation, web analytics, SEO, paid media, intent-data, ABM, and attribution tools.
* Experience launching services, entering new markets, repositioning a brand, or scaling a marketing organization.

Work Environment

* Fully remote role with occasional travel for industry events and offsite meetings

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with a disability.*

title: Director, Enterprise Communications
description:
**Who We Are**

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

**What We Build**

Our products—**Eureka Math and** Eureka Math², **Wit & Wisdom**, **Geodes**, and the newly launched **Arts & Letters ELA**—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

* **Eureka Math** is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.
* **Wit & Wisdom®** and **Arts & Letters ELA™** anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. **Geodes®** complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

**Where We’re Headed**

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.

**Job Purpose**

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Communications, the Director, Enterprise Communicationswill act as a senior leader responsible for the strategy, execution, and continuous evolution of Great Minds’ internal communications and employer brand functions. Internally, this role will shape how the organization communicates at an enterprise level, ensuring employees are informed, connected to strategy and values, and inspired by the mission and impact that drive Great Minds’ work. Externally, this role will curate, monitor, and disseminate content that tells the story of Great Minds’ mission, culture and values to support recruiting, retention, and sales. The Director will serve as the company’s chief architect of enterprise communication, setting the vision for how the company reaches, engages, and retains a dispersed, impact-driven workforce; positioning Great Minds as an employer of choice; and ensuring internal stories reach external audiences where they can reinforce our brand and reputation.

**Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership and Team Management:
  + Lead and develop the Internal Communications function, providing strategic direction, coaching, and clear accountability for goals and quality standards.
  + Set the enterprise communications vision and annual strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, culture, and the 2030 student outcomes commitment.
  + Serve as a senior strategic advisor to executive leadership and the VP, Corporate Communications, translating organizational priorities into communications approaches that build clarity, trust, and engagement.
  + Partner deeply across functions to drive alignment, inform communications, and source stories—including HR and Strategy to convey operating values and organizational direction; Research, Product, Sales, and Customer Success to surface impact data and field stories that connect employees to the difference Great Minds makes for students and educators; and Brand, Marketing, and Legal to ensure consistency, accuracy, and voice across all enterprise communications.
* Enterprise Communications:
  + Own the enterprise-wide internal communications framework—including editorial calendar, governance, channel strategy, and content standards—that keeps employees informed and connected to what matters most.
  + Lead communications for high-stakes, organization-wide moments: executive announcements, leadership transitions, strategic initiatives, transformation efforts, and town halls.
  + Ensure employees have consistent access to need-to-know operational information while also deepening their connection to Great Minds’ strategy, culture, values, and impact.
  + Build and steward a center of excellence model, equipping communications liaisons and cross-functional partners with tools, frameworks, and best practices to strengthen the quality of communications across the organization.
  + Build and operate an employee storytelling engine—partnering with teams that include Product, Research, Sales, and Customer Success to identify, develop, and distribute compelling stories of student and educator impact that connect Great Minds employees to the purpose behind their work.
  + Work closely with HR and Strategy to develop communications that actively convey Great Minds’ operating values, culture commitments, and strategic direction—ensuring employees understand not just what the organization is doing, but why it matters and how they contribute.
  + Develop and implement measurement frameworks (KPIs, engagement data, feedback loops) to continuously assess and improve internal communications effectiveness.
  + Lead the embedding of Great Minds’ refreshed enterprise brand across internal channels and communications—partnering with Brand to ensure voice, visual identity, and messaging standards are consistently reflected in all employee-facing content and experiences.
* Platform and Channel Evolution:
  + Partner with IT on Great Minds’ internal communications technology roadmap—evaluating, selecting, and optimizing platforms, tools, and formats to enhance reach, usability, and employee experience.
  + Bring technical fluency to channel strategy decisions, including intranet architecture, email platforms, video tools, and emerging collaboration and communications technologies.
  + Drive adoption and governance of communication platforms, ensuring tools are used effectively and equitably across a distributed workforce.
  + Identify gaps in current channel infrastructure and develop phased recommendations for platform evolution that serve both near-term needs and long-term scalability.
* Employer Brand and Internal Storytelling:
  + Build and lead Great Minds’ employer brand strategy, positioning the organization as a destination for mission-aligned talent and amplifying the employee experience externally.
  + Identify compelling internal stories—from educator impact to employee milestones to culture moments—and develop them into external-facing content in partnership with Media Relations and Brand.
  + Create and sustain an employee storytelling engine that amplifies authentic stories from across the organization to showcase mission impact internally and externally.
  + Collaborate with Media Relations to pitch employee and culture stories to relevant media and talent-focused outlets, expanding the reach of Great Minds’ employer brand.
  + Own Great Minds’ employer reputation strategy—including active management of Glassdoor, LinkedIn employer presence, and other third-party platforms—monitoring sentiment, responding to reviews, and developing proactive strategies to strengthen how the organization is perceived as a place to work.
  + Ensure employer brand messaging is consistent and compelling across internal and external channels, including LinkedIn, Glassdoor, and recruiting materials.
  + Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to develop communications that support the full employee lifecycle—attraction, onboarding, engagement, and retention.

**Requirements**

* 7+ years of progressive experience in communications or marketing, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise-wide strategy
* 5+ years of management experience
* Experience managing or mentoring direct reports, with a track record of developing talent and building high-functioning teams
* Experience developing or contributing to employer brand strategy, with an understanding of how internal culture stories translate to external reputation
* Demonstrated experience managing employer reputation on platforms such as Glassdoor and LinkedIn, including proactive review strategy, sentiment monitoring, and response frameworks
* Experience building employee or customer storytelling programs that surface and amplify narratives of impact across internal and external channels
* Experience partnering with brand or creative teams to embed refreshed brand identities into internal communications—including voice, visual standards, and messaging frameworks
* Proven ability to advise and influence senior executives, translating complex organizational priorities into compelling, accessible messaging
* Deep expertise in executive communications, change and transformation communications, and large-scale organizational initiatives
* Strong technical knowledge of internal communications platforms and channel ecosystems—including intranets, email platforms, video tools, and collaboration technology—with the ability to evaluate and recommend platform investments
* Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across formats, audiences, and channels
* Strong project management skills and the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in a communications function at an education or mission-driven entity
* Familiarity with media relations related to employer brand and culture storytelling
* Experience building or transforming an internal communications function, including platform migrations or channel strategy overhauls
* Track record of using data and analytics to measure communications effectiveness and drive continuous improvement

Proficiency with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Teams / Zoom, and Veeva PromoMats

description:

That’s the Kyndryl Way.

Through our company-wide volunteering and giving platform, you can donate, start fundraisers, volunteer, and search over 2 million non-profit organizations. title: Director of Production
description:
**Keep Growing with Nutrafol**
------------------------------

We’re a growing company. Everything we do, we do to help people grow into the best version of themselves. As the pioneers of hair wellness, we create clinically tested products for hair growth and provide support for people at every step of their hair journey.

Our multi-factorial approach targets key root causes of hair thinning using a patented blend of standardized vitamins, minerals and natural ingredients - and is recommended by over 7,500 physicians and hair professionals for trusted, reliable results. We never settle, and are continuously challenging existing treatments and methodologies to advance the frontier of hair science. As we help our customers grow, we grow too - by embracing individuality and differences, leading by example, and empowering ourselves and others with our passion for wellness and innovation.

Keep growing. It’s our mantra. Our commitment to helping anybody and everybody committed to realizing their own potential to grow.

#### **About you:**

Nutrafol's in-house Creative team makes everything from brand campaigns and product photography to performance ads, social content, and retail assets. As our Director of Production, you'll own how all of that work from a photography, casting and film standpoint gets made: the budgets, expenses. the schedules, the partners, and the shoot days.

This is a senior individual contributor role to start. You won't have direct reports at first. Instead, you'll lead through a network of production companies, agencies, photographers, directors, and freelancers, and through close partnership with our in-house creatives. You'll build the production function from the ground up, set the standards, and help shape how the team grows.

#### **What You'll Do:**

**Own production end to end**

* Lead production for all photo, video, and content shoots across brand, performance marketing, social, e-commerce, and retail.
* Take projects from brief to delivery: scoping, bidding, pre-production, on-set leadership, post-production, and final asset handoff.
* Act as producer on key shoots, and make sure every other shoot has the right producer.

**Manage budgets and partners**

* Build and manage the annual production budget, plus a budget for each project. Track actuals and report on spend to the SVP, Creative.
* Find, vet, and manage a roster of production companies, agencies, directors, photographers, editors, post houses, and freelance crew.
* Run bids, negotiate rates and contracts, and get the most value out of every dollar without lowering the quality of the work.
* Work with Legal and Procurement on SOWs, vendor agreements, and payments.

**Build the operating model**

* Design and run the production calendar across all creative work, balancing what the business needs with the team's capacity.
* Create repeatable workflows, templates, and best practices: production books, call sheets, approval steps, and delivery specs.
* Find ways to make more content more efficiently, such as shoots that serve several channels at once, modular content systems, and in-house studio capabilities.
* Look at and adopt new tools, including AI-assisted production and post-production workflows, where they make the work better or faster.

**Protect the brand and the business**

* Manage talent, model, and influencer usage rights, releases, and renewals. Keep a clear record of where and how long each asset can run.
* Make sure productions follow union rules (SAG-AFTRA and others where they apply), location permits, insurance, and on-set safety.
* Partner with Legal and Regulatory early in the process so that claims, testimonials, and before-and-after content meet our standards for a health and wellness brand.
* Oversee how finished assets are organized, labeled, and stored in our DAM so the whole company can find and use them.

**Partner across the company**

* Work closely with Creative Directors, Art Directors, Designers, Copywriters, and Brand teams so the work looks the way it was meant to.
* Partner with Growth, Social, E-commerce, Retail, and Product Marketing to understand what assets they need and when.
* Bring production feasibility, cost, and timing into the conversation early, during concept development.

#### **What You Bring:**

* 10+ years of production experience, with at least 3 years at a senior producer, head of production, or director level.
* Experience at an in-house brand team, a creative agency, or a production company. Ideally a mix.
* A track record of producing large-scale photo and video campaigns as well as high-volume content for performance and social channels.
* Strong budget management skills, with experience owning a multimillion-dollar annual production budget.
* A deep network of production partners, crew, and talent, and the judgment to match the right partner to each project.

* Experience setting up production processes and systems where none existed.
